title: The use of ChatGPT in the digital era: Perspectives on chatbot implementation
extended_summary:
This paper examines how educators and students perceive the use of ChatGPT in education during the digital era. Rather than testing an instructional intervention with measured learning outcomes, the study asks what participants think ChatGPT can do in educational settings, what concerns they have, and how it might fit into day-to-day academic support.

The study used a qualitative design with in-depth interviews and content analysis. It sampled 25 participants from higher education institutions in Krabi, Thailand: ten educators and 15 students. Participants were selected purposively and had current experience with ChatGPT. The interview protocol focused on perceived impacts on learning, workload reduction, accuracy of chatbot responses, the possible loss of human interaction, privacy and security, and how ChatGPT might be improved or balanced with human support.

Findings were generally positive. Educators and students saw ChatGPT as useful for answering routine questions, giving immediate feedback, generating ideas, summarising texts, and supporting independent learning. Educators especially valued its potential to reduce workload and free time for more complex teaching tasks. At the same time, participants raised concerns about inaccurate or incomplete responses, bias in training data, reduced personal interaction, and data privacy risks. The paper concludes that ChatGPT can be a helpful educational resource if used alongside human guidance, critical evaluation, and stronger privacy protections.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative interview study with purposive sampling and content analysis, so it provides contextual insight but limited causal credibility. It is peer-reviewed, but it does not test an intervention experimentally or with a comparison group.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports perceived benefits such as workload reduction and immediate feedback, but provides no quantitative impact estimates or demonstrated outcomes. Its overall impact is therefore suggestive and unclear rather than measurable.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT used as a conversational educational assistant for students and educators to answer routine questions, provide immediate feedback, generate ideas, and support academic tasks in higher education.

finding.finding_summary: Participants reported that ChatGPT reduced educator workload by answering routine student questions and freeing time for higher-order tasks such as lesson planning and individualized support. This was based on qualitative interviews with n=25 participants (10 educators, 15 students) in higher education in Krabi, Thailand; no effect size was reported.
finding.measure: Perceived educator workload reduction and task efficiency from qualitative interviews

finding.finding_summary: Educators and students described ChatGPT as increasing confidence, engagement, and motivation because it provided immediate answers and support outside classroom hours. At the same time, participants worried about reduced personal interaction, which could weaken rapport and belonging in the classroom; no quantitative effect size was reported.
finding.measure: Perceived engagement, motivation, confidence, and sense of personal connection from interviews

finding.finding_summary: The paper argues that ChatGPT may improve educational practice through faster feedback and support, but also raises institutional concerns about accuracy, privacy, and data security. These are qualitative findings from interviews and discussion rather than a quantitative policy evaluation; no effect size was reported.
finding.measure: Perceptions of institutional benefits and risks, including privacy, accuracy, and governance concerns
